Dressers
DRES-erz
n. pl. (in vine dressers, those who tend and prune vines)
From dress, Old French dresser, to set in order or make straight. The Authorized Version uses the plural in vine dressers, of the men Uzziah employed in the mountains and in Carmel, for he loved husbandry.

Biblical Definition

Also he built towers in the desert, and digged many wells: for he had much cattle, both in the low country, and in the plains: husbandmen also, and vine dressers in the mountains, and in Carmel: for he loved husbandry. The Chronicler gives Uzziah a long and admiring paragraph — towers, wells, herds, vineyards, engines invented by cunning men to shoot arrows and great stones, and a name that spread far abroad, for he was marvellously helped, till he was strong. Then the hinge of his life, and one of the most quoted verses in Chronicles: but when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction: for he transgressed against the LORD his God, and went into the temple of the LORD to burn incense upon the altar of incense. Eighty priests withstood him, the leprosy rose in his forehead, and he was a leper to the day of his death, dwelling in a several house. The vine dressers stand in the good half of that paragraph. God gave him the wells and the vineyards and the victories, and the very strength that came from them became the occasion of his ruin. The Lord's own use of the trade is gentler and more searching: the dresser of the vineyard who begs one more year for the barren fig tree.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): one who dresses; a vine dresser, one who tends and trims vines; in Scripture, the labourers Uzziah set in the mountains and in Carmel.

expand to see more

DRESSER, n. One who dresses; one who is employed in preparing, trimming or adjusting anything.

VINEDRESSER, n. One who dresses, trims, prunes and cultivates vines.

HUSBANDRY, n. The business of a farmer; tillage or cultivation of the soil.

PRUNE, v.t. To lop or cut off the superfluous branches of trees, to make them bear better fruit.

HUSBANDMAN, n. A farmer; a cultivator or tiller of the ground.

Key Scripture

2Ch 26:10 — "Also he built towers in the desert, and digged many wells: for he had much cattle, both in the low country, and in the plains: husbandmen also, and vine dressers in the mountains, and in Carmel: for he loved husbandry."

2Ch 26:16 — "But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction: for he transgressed against the LORD his God, and went into the temple of the LORD to burn incense upon the altar of incense."

Luk 13:7 — "Then said he unto the dresser of his vineyard, Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none: cut it down; why cumbereth it the ground?"

Joh 15:1 — "I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman."

Modern Corruption

Success is treated as a stable condition rather than a season of peculiar danger; the Chronicler puts Uzziah's ruin in a single clause — when he was strong, his heart was lifted up.

expand to see more

2 Chronicles 26:16 is the sentence the dictionary would hang in every prosperous church office. Uzziah did nothing wrong while he was weak. He sought God in the days of Zechariah, and as long as he sought the LORD, God made him to prosper. The danger arrived with the prosperity, and it arrived in the specific form of a man deciding that his standing entitled him to a priest's office. Strength did not corrupt him by making him wicked in the ordinary sense; it made him think the boundaries were for other people.

The priests' response is worth as much as the warning. Azariah and eighty priests that were valiant men withstood the king to his face and told him to go out of the sanctuary, and the leprosy rose while the censer was in his hand. Courage in the ministry means telling a strong man the one thing everyone around him has stopped saying. And the Lord's parable gives the other side of the trade: the dresser pleading for one more year over a barren tree, digging about it and dunging it, which is what patient pastoral labour actually looks like when the owner has every right to cut.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew korem (H3755), a vinedresser; 'ikkar (H406), a husbandman or ploughman; gabahh (H1361), to be high or lifted up.

expand to see more

Hebrew korem (H3755) — a vinedresser, a tender of vines; the vine dressers of 2 Chronicles 26:10.

Hebrew 'ikkar (H406) — a husbandman, a tiller of the soil; husbandmen also.

Hebrew 'adamah (H127) — the ground, the soil; he loved husbandry, literally the ground.

Hebrew gabahh (H1361) — to be lofty, to be exalted; his heart was lifted up to his destruction.

Greek georgos (G1092) — a tiller of the soil, a vinedresser, a husbandman; my Father is the husbandman.

Usage

"“husbandmen also, and vine dressers in the mountains” — the occurrence, in Uzziah's prosperity."

"“when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction” — the hinge of his life."

"“said he unto the dresser of his vineyard” — the Lord's use of the trade."
